correctness.rationale: Mechanical dissipation on (y,v₁,v₂) is nonpositive; the invariant subset with both velocities zero is just the origin, yielding a Hurwitz linear drift and unique stationary covariance. Stationarity gives c=E[yv₁]=E[yv₂], and elimination of E[v₁v₂] and the two velocity variances gives c=(T₁−T₂)/D with D=γ₁+γ₂+k[m₁/γ₁+m₂/γ₂+(m₁−m₂)²/(γ₁m₂+γ₂m₁)]. Algebra agrees with the stated J=kc and reduces fixed-sum maximization to F_r(p). The current vanishes at both endpoints. The positive term in (log F_r)'' is smaller than p⁻² for r>1 and (1−p)⁻² for r<1, so the interior stationary point is the unique maximum. Independently expanded the derivative numerator and both resultants. A direct ceiling proof also follows by setting p₀=1/2−√7/28: P_r(p₀)=(29√7−28)(r−(16+5√7)/9)²(r+(23−8√7)/9)/1568, nonnegative with just one positive zero. Strict log-concavity therefore gives p_*≥p₀ with equality only at that ratio; exchanging masses gives the upper bound and its reciprocal equality. The exact midpoint derivative gives the side of 1/2 for each r, and evaluating the two currents in the worked example agrees with the printed numbers.
residual_risks: Stationarity is asserted only for the relative variables. The optimization uses physical frictions, not friction divided by mass. No finite-time or pinned-system conclusion follows.
The packaged numerical Lyapunov tests use fixed positive bath temperatures, despite broader wording about randomized parameters. The derivation covers arbitrary stated temperatures.

originality.rationale: The inspected transport and damping-optimization sources do not give an equivalent full fixed-budget result. Classical oscillator current formulas are antecedents, not themselves the optimal allocation or its uniform sharp ceiling. The closest indexed free dimer optimizes a different quantity and control, and the thermal near match optimizes a mass in a pinned chain. The distinct claim is the unique fixed-sum friction optimizer, its mass-only dependence and its universal sharp extremum.

value.rationale: For a natural resource constraint on two contacts, the analysis solves the full unequal-mass design problem and bounds the greatest adjustment required over all mass ratios. Independence from stiffness, budget and temperatures, plus exact equality at intermediate reciprocal ratios rather than at extreme mass disparity, is informative beyond a routine covariance calculation or one small example.
residual_risks: The objective is only expected stationary heat current in the unpinned classical model; no claim about efficiency, fluctuations, other pinning or realistic contact constraints.
